The fixed circuit ran on garnet:mock with 100 shots. It returned {"00": 53, "11": 47} for measurement key m, with bits in the order (QB1, QB2). I submitted 1 job.

The original circuit had two bugs.
1. QB25 does not exist. Garnet has only QB1 to QB20. The live architecture lists cz pairs for QB1 with QB2 and QB4 only. I changed the partner qubit to QB2.
2. "cx" is not a native IQM operation. Garnet accepts prx, cz and measure. I built the CNOT from native gates. The sequence is prx(-pi/2, phase pi/2) on QB2, then cz on (QB2, QB1), then prx(pi/2, phase pi/2) on QB2.

I kept the first prx(pi/2, phase pi/2) on QB1. That gate is a Ry(pi/2), and it puts QB1 into superposition. The measure on QB1 and QB2 with key "m" is also unchanged.

The fixed instructions are: prx QB1 (pi/2, pi/2), prx QB2 (-pi/2, pi/2), cz [QB2, QB1], prx QB2 (pi/2, pi/2), measure [QB1, QB2] key m.

The mock gave only 00 and 11 in this run. The docs say the mock returns random results, so this run does not prove the Bell pair works on real hardware. The script is at /Users/claytonchancey/Desktop/quantum/.claude/worktrees/wf_1a6926f8-f6c-59/scratch/bell_fixed.py.
